about.intro: A 24-hour digital twin of road traffic in Lucca and the surrounding plain (about 16 × 13 km, from Ponte a Moriano to the A11). Every vehicle is simulated individually; road colours show the hourly average from the simulation, and the moving vehicles replay a 90-second slice recorded at half past each hour. It is a model calibrated to published counts, not a live traffic feed.
about.network: OpenStreetMap road graph converted with SUMO netconvert: about 1,700 km of road, 10,332 directed links, signalised and priority junctions, roundabouts, OSM turn restrictions and lane counts. Inside the Walls the ZTL is closed to general traffic and open only to permit holders, taxis, buses and deliveries. Speed limits are 50 km/h in built-up areas, 70–90 km/h outside, and 130 km/h on the A11.
about.demand: Tour-based synthetic demand for about 115,000 residents in the study area (ISTAT 1 Jan 2025: Lucca 89,002; part of Capannori, 46,644; part of Porcari, 8,845). Homes and destinations come from 50,000 building volumes and land use. Trip timing follows Italian patterns: school runs at 7:30–8:15, pick-ups around 13:00 and 16:15, a lunch return home for part of the workforce, and an evening peak. Destinations follow a gravity model. On top of that: commuters and visitors entering through 62 boundary roads, through traffic on the A11, vans and lorries, and ZTL permit traffic. Weekday: 339,525 vehicle trips. Saturday: 299,048 (0.88 × weekday, the ratio measured on SR439).
about.sim: Eclipse SUMO 1.28 microscopic simulation: Krauss car-following, LC2013 lane changing, 1-second steps. Route choice is dynamic: every vehicle routes on current travel times when it departs and reroutes every 5 minutes, an approximation of dynamic user equilibrium. Vehicles stuck for more than 5 minutes are teleported, as is standard in SUMO. Teleports: 5,751 on the weekday and 4,026 on Saturday.
about.hotspots: Junctions are grouped into clusters: roundabouts, and nodes linked by edges shorter than 45 m. Each cluster is scored by the vehicle-hours lost on its approach links, measured as SUMO time loss against free-flow speed. Insertion queues on the boundary roads are excluded. The ranking uses daily totals; the 3D columns show the selected hour.
about.limits: Counts are sparse and dated (2017–2021). The model is about 10–15% high on SR439 and SS12 and 25–35% low on the eastern Pesciatina and Viale Europa corridors. Signal plans are not public, so SUMO-generated actuated plans are used. About 1% of vehicles get teleported out of local deadlocks. One junction at the Lucca Ovest toll is left out of the ranking because its delay comes from lane-change blocking on very short links, a known SUMO artefact. Parking search, buses, bicycles, roadworks, incidents and events (such as Lucca Comics & Games) are not modelled. Treat absolute delays as indicative and the ranking of critical points as the main result.
